bull.b: Debt is only ~$4.4M with debt-to-equity near 0.28, while equity is positive at approximately $15.7M after prior negative-equity years. This provides a more resilient base for funding regulatory work and commercialization, although continued losses could erode it if cash burn persists.

TTM gross margin rose to about 58% from roughly 54% in 2025 and 44–49% in 2022–2024. The improvement indicates better unit economics and could support future operating leverage as volume grows, even though deeply negative operating margins show scale benefits are not yet realized.

An independent blinded survey found 96% surgeon interest in NXT-41x, 100% willingness to use it for high-risk patients, and 92% willingness to champion it to hospital VACs. Such broad stated demand supports adoption potential if regulatory clearance and launch execution follow.

bear.b: TTM revenue fell approximately 24% versus the prior annual period and has stepped down materially from 2021 levels. A shrinking sales base makes it harder to absorb the existing cost structure, delays operating breakeven, and leaves future profitability dependent on successful NXT-41x commercialization.

Operating cash flow was about -$44.0M TTM and free cash flow about -$45.5M, with FCF deteriorating roughly 74% versus 2025. Persistent cash consumption means the business is not self-funding and could require financing, dilution, or debt unless core operations improve materially.

Projected funding and the commercial plan depend partly on a $5M facility tranche, an $8M escrow release, and up to $3M in milestones, while NXT-41 and NXT-41x clearances remain pending. This exposes runway and launch timing to execution and regulatory outcomes.
